concept.title: Ordered Lists (Numbered)
concept.abstract: This section covers Ordered Lists in DOCX — items presented in a defined sequence where position is significant — and twenty-one scenarios grouped across six categories: consecutive and discontinuous numbered lists as procedures and workflows, single-item numbered lists, two-level and three-level nested numbered lists, and interrupted numbered lists where an admonition, paragraph, image, table, or bullet list appears between items. The converter maps each ordered list to <ol><li> in concept and reference topics, or to <steps><step><cmd> in task topics, based on the heading classification and content context.

conbody.p: An ordered list presents items in a defined sequence where the position of each item is significant. The ordered lists are universally used for step-by-step procedures, installation instructions, and ranked items.

For the reader, a numbered list communicates that sequence is contractual — item 2 depends on item 1 being completed, and performing the items out of order produces an incorrect or unsafe result. It is also a navigational reference that lets a reader say "I am on step 4" and return to the correct position after an interruption.

The list level is controlled by the Increase and Decrease Indent buttons, determines nesting depth: level 1 is the top level, level 2 is the first nested level, level 3 is the second, and so on. The list level assigned by list controls is what drives the nesting structure in the DITA output.

In task topics, the instructions or procedures becomes a <steps><step><cmd> structures inside <taskbody>.
